quarterly_data.signal: Memory revenue and bookings increased meaningfully in Q1, driven by strong DRAM and high bandwidth memory demand as customers ramp capacity investments for AI; system shipments to memory reached the highest level since the fourth quarter of 2023. Korea was the second-largest region at 28% of total revenues as a result of higher memory sales.
quarterly_data.figure: Korea 28% of total revenues; memory shipments highest since the fourth quarter of 2023

quarterly_data.signal: Completed the systems evaluation for the Purion high current system ordered by a leading North American memory manufacturer (unnamed) and is working to drive adoption across technology nodes and regions. Memory expected to be a little softer sequentially in Q2, but strong full-year 2026 growth with momentum into 2027; that growth is all DRAM, with not much NAND embedded because NAND makers focus on vertical scaling, which does not need much incremental implant.

No meaningful change from any memory mix shift away from HBM: customers are still trying to build out HBM capacity and DRAM for AI. CEO: HBM is essentially DRAM stacked, so implant intensity does not change much between DRAM and HBM (or NAND, or node to node); only the mix of high energy, high current and medium current differs.

Q1 2026 revenue $199 million (system revenue approximately $126 million, CS&I $73 million), EPS $0.72, slightly above expectations, including a one-time $5 million customer settlement headwind to system revenue. CS&I grew more than 30% year over year on service, consumables and system upgrades. Gross margin 40.7% (outlook 41%), operating margin 11.7%, adjusted EBITDA $27.7 million. China rose to 40% of revenue from 32% in the prior quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $199 million; systems ~$126 million; CS&I $73 million; EPS $0.72; gross margin 40.7%; China 40%

quarterly_data.signal: Bookings roughly flat sequentially at $128 million, the second consecutive quarter of firming order rates (second consecutive quarter of year-over-year growth on a trailing 12-month basis), driven by memory and silicon carbide demand offset by softer general mature. Backlog $453 million at quarter end. Management will not guide quarterly bookings.

Q2 outlook: revenue approximately $205 million with a higher general mature mix and lower memory and silicon carbide mix; gross margin approximately 43%; opex approximately $59 million; adjusted EBITDA approximately $34 million; EPS approximately $0.90. Full-year 2026 revenue still expected approximately flat versus 2025, second-half weighted on improving silicon carbide and continued memory strength, with a return to growth set up for 2027; full-year gross margin in the low to mid 40% range, opex approximately $60 million per quarter, tax rate approximately 15%.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue ~$205 million; gross margin ~43%; EPS ~$0.90; FY2026 revenue approximately flat

quarterly_data.signal: Power / silicon carbide: shipments moderated sequentially but bookings strengthened and customer engagement on capacity plans rose; at SEMICON China focus was on super junction development, high energy implant, channeling and the transition to 200 mm. Rising SiC penetration and content per EV (800 V systems: traction inverter, DC-DC, onboard charging, AC compressor) and use in white goods. In AI data centers management sees both materials: gallium nitride inside the rack as it moves to 800 V, silicon carbide as power steps down from the grid (13 kV or more) toward the rack; data-center SiC is still low volume relative to EVs and its size is TBD.
Introduced the next-generation high current product Purion H6 in Q1 and is engaging multiple customers on it; secured a high current win with a new customer in China.

General mature: Q1 bookings were softer and 2026 general mature is still expected down year over year, but utilization rates are rising (spares and consumables continued to improve) with stabilizing auto, recovering industrial and growing AI data center demand; management feels better about 2027 than three months earlier. Advanced logic generated no system revenue in Q1. For data-center optics, Axcelis does not take part in laser manufacturing; the silicon modulation unit needs an isolation implant, a small but real photonics application.

Pending Veeco merger still expected to close in the second half of 2026; approval from China's State Administration of Market Regulation is the only approval remaining. Free cash flow $16 million including $12 million of cash transaction expenses for the merger; no share repurchases; $570 million of cash equivalents and marketable securities at quarter end.
quarterly_data.figure: free cash flow $16 million; cash and securities $570 million
